description: Five sharded, character-specific numeric parameter tables sharing FGameDataTableRow_CharacterUnique. FGameDataTableRow_Character::Id_CharacterUnique supplies an ordered list of row keys; AGameCharacter resolves them against the manager's merged CharacterUniqueDataTables and caches the pointers in UniqueRows. Runtime code reads FloatValue as untyped per-row slots through IGameActorInterface, so each slot's meaning and units are defined by the calling character/action rather than by a shared field schema.

ID.simple: Row key for a character-wide tuning block or a named technique/variant block.
ID.technical: The exported key is ID; the native UPROPERTY is FName Id (ImportKeyField=Id in every shard). Each shard's Rows map is keyed by it: examples include CP_050 and CP_020_ATTACKA for character and technique blocks. FGameDataTableRow_Character::Id_CharacterUnique is TArray<FName>; AGameCharacter::ResolveDataRows iterates it and calls GameCharacter_FindOptionalRow over the five-table array. The finder skips FName None and calls FindRow<TRow>(Id, TEXT(""), false) in shard order, so an unmatched name inserts nullptr and a duplicate would resolve to the first matching shard. The cached pointer array preserves the Id_CharacterUnique order (AGameCharacter +0x420).

FloatValue.simple: Ordered array of untyped numeric tuning values for that character/technique row.
FloatValue.technical: Declared as TArray<float>; the row constructor is empty, so 14 entries are a property of the supplied data, not a C++-level fixed size. All 195 exported rows in all five shards have exactly 14 entries. AGameCharacter::GetCharacterUniqueFloatValue(ValueIndex, RowIndex) (retail 0x14126d6f0) dereferences UniqueRows.GetData()[RowIndex]->FloatValue.GetData()[ValueIndex] with no bounds or null checks; the reconstructed body is byte-matched to retail (27/27 bytes). Callers use literal slots 0..13 and level/state-selected index tables; some cast a float to int32 for counts or enum selectors. Units and sentinel rules are established only at each call site (seconds, world-space distances, angles/FOV, counts, cost or rate multipliers); for example CP_160 treats row 3 slot 0 as an unlimited range when negative. Zero is not a table-wide 'unused' sentinel.

notes: Exported shards are CharacterUniqueDataTable1 (30 rows), 2 (24), 3 (60), 4 (55) and 5 (26): 195 rows total. All use RowStruct GameDataTableRow_CharacterUnique and ImportKeyField=Id, have the same two exported fields, and have no duplicate row IDs. The manager creates DataTable primary-asset loaders for the five numbered tables and appends the resolved non-null UDataTables in that order to CharacterUniqueDataTables (DTM +0x570); the ordered finder therefore gives the first shard precedence.

Every one of the 48 exported CharacterDataTable rows has nine Id_CharacterUnique slots. All 195 non-None IDs resolve to the 195 unique rows; every unused slot is the FName None and becomes a null UniqueRows entry. RowIndex is the index into that nine-slot cache, not a shard number, and ValueIndex is the FloatValue element. Because the accessor dereferences both arrays directly, a missing/None row or out-of-range index faults rather than returning a default.

Slot meaning is per consumer. FGameCharacterAction::MakeUniqueCameraRequest reads slots 0..2 as camera offset, 3/4 as limit angles, 5 as FOV, 6 as blend time, 7 as an easing selector (0 Linear, 1 EaseIn, 2 EaseOut, 3 EaseInOut), and 8..10 as orbit angles. CP_050 row 0 uses slots 0..3 for gauge cost, maximum count, charge-rate divisor and guard hold time; CP_070 selects row-0 multiplier slots 2..9 from owner-minus-target cursed-energy level; CP_230, CP_240 and CN_122 also index through small runtime tables keyed by level, passive or shot index. CN_122 and CN_250 read rows as high as row 8 and slots up to 13, so trailing zeros are not inherently unused.

The interface name is shared but the backing table is not: IGameActorInterface::GetCharacterUniqueFloatValue's default implementation returns 0.0, AGameCharacter's override reads this table, while AGameShikigami's override reads ShikigamiUniqueDataTable through Id_ShikigamiUnique. Consequently FCN_050 and FCN_070 shikigami action calls to the same method are not CharacterUniqueDataTable consumers. FGameTrapAction::GetUniqueFloat can be an indirect consumer when its spawner source is an AGameCharacter: it returns 0 without a source interface, otherwise forwards to that source's slot-155 accessor.

The supplied export set contains only the five numbered shards; no locale-specific CharacterUnique variant was provided. Consumer roles here come from reconstructed C++ tied to retail RVAs, and the accessor body itself is byte-matched; no retail Blueprint graph was supplied, so no Blueprint-only reader or additional retail row outside the export is asserted.

usages.detail: Resolves CharacterUniqueDataTable1-5 as primary assets and appends them, in order, to CharacterUniqueDataTables (+0x570); null tables are filtered out.
ResolveDataRows walks Id_CharacterUnique and caches an ordered row pointer (or nullptr) per ID in UniqueRows.
MakeUniqueCameraRequest maps slots 0..10 of the selected row to camera offset, angle limits, FOV, blend time, easing selector and orbit angles.
TickLimitless uses row 0 slots 1 (maximum count), 3 (guard hold time), 2 (charge-rate denominator) and 0 (gauge cost).
Owner-minus-target cursed-energy level selects row-0 multiplier slots 2..9 for two pending bonus accumulators.
Uses literal and runtime-table-selected value indices across rows 0..6 for timing, range, radius, position and shot parameters.
Indirect path: trap actions forward GetUniqueFloat to the spawner's IGameActorInterface accessor, or return 0 when no source interface exists.
